name: RankItem
tagline: A web tool for building ranked lists and tier-style rankings by comparing items head to head.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Ranking tools are one of the most one-shottable categories in existence: the whole product is a pairwise comparison loop, a sort, and a shareable result. An agent can build a local version with Elo or merge-insertion sort, image uploads, drag to reorder, and a PNG export in a single session. What you will not get for free is the polish, the mobile touch handling, and whatever public list gallery the hosted version has. If your rankings are private or one-off, that gallery is worthless to you anyway. Nothing here needs a server beyond static hosting and localStorage.
coreLoopDIY: Paste or upload a list of items, answer a series of 'which is better' pairwise prompts, get a ranked list or tier board you can export as an image or JSON.
requirements: optional image files for list items
whatYouLose: Public shareable links other people can open and vote on
Any prebuilt template lists so you do not have to type 40 items yourself
Mobile-tuned drag and drop, which is genuinely fiddly to get right
Someone else fixing it when the export renders text at the wrong offset
Whatever community or discovery feed exists around published rankings
moatNotes: The only durable part of a ranking site is other people's lists and the traffic that comes with them. For personal use that part is dead weight.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because typing your items into a box that already works beats spending an evening on comparison logic, and because publishing a link that a hundred friends can open is the actual point for most users. Hosted ranking tools also absorb the boring parts: image hosting, thumbnail cropping, share card generation, mobile touch targets. If you want a shareable artifact rather than a private ordering, paying is rational.
notes: Pairwise ranking is the hello-world of interaction design, and that is not an insult, it just means you should build it.
prompt:
Build a local-first pairwise ranking web app. Empty folder, no backend.

Stack, non negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, plain CSS modules, no UI framework, no Tailwind. Persistence is localStorage only. No accounts, no server, no analytics, no telemetry.

Core flow:
1. Setup screen: name the ranking, paste items one per line into a textarea, or add items individually with an optional image (store images as base64 data URLs in localStorage, warn if total exceeds 4MB).
2. Compare screen: show two items side by side with a keyboard shortcut (left arrow, right arrow, and space for 'too close to call'). Show progress as 'comparison 12 of ~40'.
3. Use merge-insertion style sorting driven by user answers so the number of comparisons is roughly n log n, not n squared. Treat 'too close to call' as a tie and keep existing relative order. Persist partial progress so a refresh resumes mid-session.
4. Result screen: ordered list with rank numbers and images if present. Allow manual drag to reorder afterward using the HTML5 drag events, with keyboard alternatives (alt+up, alt+down).
5. Tier mode toggle: bucket the sorted result into S/A/B/C/D tiers with adjustable cut points via sliders.

Export: render the result to a PNG via an offscreen canvas that you draw yourself, no html2canvas dependency. Also export and import JSON so a ranking is portable.

Out of scope: sharing links, public galleries, multi-user voting, cloud sync, image CDN, auth.

Requirements: works offline after first load, keyboard accessible throughout, sane behavior for 2 items and for 200 items. Include a seeded demo ranking so the app is not empty on first run. Write a README with run instructions and a short note on how the sort works. No secrets needed, but if you add any config use a .env file and commit a .env.example only.
